findings.title: BuildIndex scoped lock allows concurrent builds for the same key
findings.body: The lock was moved from the entire BuildIndex path to only the final cache insertion. However searchSupport.getOrCreateIndex has no per-key synchronization: two callers that both see GetIndex return nil for the same NamespacedResource can now run BuildIndex concurrently. For file-backed indexes this means two calls to bleve.New on the same directory can open/modify the same bleve data files concurrently, causing corruption or an error; for memory indexes one built index is leaked and the cache is last-writer-wins. Use a per-key lock/singleflight or re-check the cache after acquiring the lock.

findings.title: Search init worker goroutines race on shared variables
findings.body: Inside searchSupport.init the errgroup workers are limited but still concurrent. Each goroutine executes `totalBatchesIndexed++` and `_, _, err = s.build(...)` on variables shared with all other workers. These are unsynchronized writes to the same memory, so this is a data race. The `err` capture is also semantically wrong: one goroutine can overwrite the outer `err` before another returns it, causing a build failure to be reported as success or vice versa. Declare `err` locally with `:=` in the closure and use an atomic counter for totalBatchesIndexed.

findings.title: Search watch goroutine panics on closed event channel
findings.body: The goroutine started in searchSupport.init reads from the write-events channel with `v := <-events` and immediately calls `s.handleEvent(watchctx, v)` without checking the channel-open boolean. The SQL watcher closes its stream when the backend stops (`defer close(stream)` in the poller), after which a receive returns a nil *WrittenEvent. `handleEvent` dereferences `evt.Type`, causing a nil-pointer panic that can crash the process during shutdown. Check `v, ok := <-events` and return on `!ok`, and wire the loop to a cancellable context.

findings.title: Resource version returned by build is discarded so watch events can be lost
findings.body: s.build returns the last resource version read while listing that namespace, specifically so a watch can resume after it. searchSupport.init discards that value with `_`. After all indexes are built it calls WatchWriteEvents, which in the SQL backend starts from the latest RV at that moment. Any write that lands after a namespace was listed but before WatchWriteEvents captures the baseline becomes the baseline itself and is never emitted to the search index, leaving the search index missing that update until a later event or rebuild. Keep the per-resource RV and pass it to the watcher, or start watching before the build and buffer events.

findings.title: Postgres storage server integration test is skipped
findings.body: This PR adds a skip for the postgres backend in TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer, with a TODO to fix the test later. Since the PR changes unified storage initialization from lazy to eager, postgres coverage for this startup path is removed exactly when it is most likely to catch startup or indexing regressions. Fix the test or ensure equivalent postgres coverage runs in CI.

findings.title: Eager Init failure returns without cleaning up partial startup
findings.body: NewResourceServer now calls s.Init(ctx) before returning the server. If Init fails, it returns nil and discards s, but Init can have partially succeeded: lifecycle.Init may have opened the backend, and search.init may have already started its watcher goroutine before a later step such as initWatcher fails. Since no server is returned, the caller cannot call Stop, and s.cancel/lifecycle.Stop are not invoked on this error path, leaking the DB lifecycle and background watchers. On Init failure, cancel s.ctx and stop the lifecycle if it was initialized before returning.
